verdicts.correction: COBOLNET1542 is SHARED by the SR2, SR3 and SR4 placement checks (DataBinder.AnyLengthValidateUnit), so the bare-code .err files do not assert THIS rule's violation. Concretely, for the -unreferenced leg a regression that classified the FUNCTION-ID as a contained program would reject M under SR3 with the same code 1542, and the test would still pass. The harness is a case-insensitive substring match, and the corpus already uses message-bearing .err files for shared codes (precedent: the misc-p2 inherits-cycle overturn). Replace l1c01-any-length-function-returning.err with: COBOLNET1542: data item 'R': in a FUNCTION the subject of an ANY LENGTH clause shall be referenced in the procedure division header as a formal parameter with the BY REFERENCE phrase   and l1c01-any-length-function-unreferenced.err with the same text for data item 'M' (both are the exact emitted text at 2002/2014/2023). The programs, the reject-at lists (2002 2014 2023) and the §13.18.2.3 4) citation are otherwise correct: SR1 and SR2 both hold, and only SR3 b) (not applicable to a function) would admit the RETURNING leg.

`IF A = B AND NOT NOT C` is rejected by the §8.8.4.12.2 GENERAL FORMAT before any implied insertion happens. After the logical operator, the format admits exactly ONE slot {NOT | simple-relational-operator | extended-relational-operator} and then object-1, so two NOTs followed by a bare object (where 'NOT C' is not a relational operator and C is not a condition-name) match no alternative. The writer's own reason for dropping `A = B AND NOT NOT < C` ('rejected by the general format, not by SR2') applies equally to this witness. SR2 is therefore not the only reason for the rejection, and the .err COBOL0001 ('cannot parse construct near NOT') is a generic parse error that any grammar without an abbreviation rule would also produce. So this is not a single-rule negative for SR2. Either find a format-legal abbreviation whose EXPANSION breaks Table 5 (I could not construct one: every format-legal expansion gives '[NOT] (subject op object)', which Table 5 admits), or re-disposition the row as satisfied-by-construction by the general format, with no negative golden.

The only soft one is the bare-word check `12.3.7.4 "ALSO"`, which resolves to 7) but quotes item i). The real ALSO text ('assigned to the same ordinal position', item 6 of rule 7) also checks OK at §12.3.7.4 7), so the clause number is right; the writer should swap in that quote. (2) I derived every .out line by hand from the source. MOVE implied point: 00123, 00987, 00, 345, '  7', '1 23'. Edited truncation: 999.99<-12345.678='345.67', ZZ9.9<-1.99='  1.9', $$$9<-12345='$345' (3 digit positions after the first $), $$,$$9.99<-12.3='   $12.30' (the comma inside the floating string is blanked, currency lands before the first nonzero digit). SQRT(2) to 34 digits is ...724209698 with the next digit 0, truncated to 30 decimals = 1414213562373095048801688724209, and a binary64 result differs from the 17th digit. Alternate keys: W2 is 22 and never stored, W3 is 02 on the DUPLICATES key, and the REWRITE to BBBB collides with 0003 so it is 22 and 0004 keeps AAAB. Under FOLD, aB equals Ab and Ac does not (c is unlisted and falls after the listed characters). Ordinals come from the CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-8 text (code unit + 1, X"FF"=256, euro=8365, N"A"=66), not from observation. Group sizes come from the DOC-A.1-6 text (3-byte COMP+X group, filler bits after a bit item, national 2 bytes per item 33). (3) Discrimination: a slack byte before the first item changes LEN-G and G1-AT-1. EBCDIC or 1..256 numbering changes the 2002 ordinal lines. A contained program that ignored its own OPTIONS would print binary64 digits on the SD lines. NFKC-folding U+FF02 into '"' would give LEN-FW=3. (4) Editions: 85 goldens use only 85-plus-intrinsics constructs (the corpus already has FUNCTION in 85). The 2002 dirs need X/N literals, CHAR-NATIONAL, key-level COLLATING SEQUENCE OF (the project gates it at 2002, cf. pb703), and TYPEDEF STRONG/BIT/BYTE-LENGTH. The 2014 dir needs STANDARD-DECIMAL. Arithmetic negatives: the reject-at years are correct, and the two-alternatives case correctly omits 2002, where STANDARD-DECIMAL does not exist. (5) As a sanity check only, I compiled all drafts with the built compiler: every positive matches its .out, and every negative is rejected at its listed years with the stated code. Residual weakness, not overturned: the two NATIVE legs of l1c01_arithmetic_clause_forms print a window that also contains the SD value, so they pin that the IS-omitted NATIVE form parses, not which engine it selects.
